### Welcome

I am Thyagi, a computational geoscientist specialising in geodynamics and geophysics. My research is driven by a fundamental question: why do large earthquakes occur? I address this by combining numerical modelling, geophysical observations, and computational methods to investigate dynamic Earth processes.

My active research focuses on megathrust earthquakes, subduction dynamics, mantle convection, and fault representation in geodynamic models. I am also interested in structural geology, especially modelling faults and fault networks that connect deep Earth dynamics with observable geological processes at the surface.

To study these problems, I use open-source computational tools on high-performance computing systems, often spanning thousands of CPU cores, to model Earth processes across wide spatial and temporal scales. I am an active developer and contributor to Underworld software and tools for geodynamic modelling and Earth science applications.

<script>
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
  const rotator = document.querySelector("[data-updates-rotator]");
  if (!rotator) return;

  const cards = Array.from(rotator.querySelectorAll(".update-card"));
  if (cards.length <= 1) return;

  let activeIndex = 0;
  const showCard = (nextIndex) => {
    cards.forEach((card, index) => {
      const isActive = index === nextIndex;
      card.classList.toggle("is-active", isActive);
      card.toggleAttribute("hidden", !isActive);
    });
  };

  showCard(activeIndex);
  window.setInterval(() => {
    activeIndex = (activeIndex + 1) % cards.length;
    showCard(activeIndex);
  }, 10000);
});
</script>
:::
